items.note: Answers directly: Pro churn did jump (1 cancel in 38 account-months in Apr–Jul vs 10 in 31 in Aug–Sep), but the data can't show the price increase caused it. Uses Basic as a comparison and lists other possible causes. Counts check out against the data. One flaw: the table lumps pre-August Pro accounts under 'Pro at 49', even though 8 of them show 69.
Removes the 5 @ourco.test rows and notes they would have inflated the August jump.
Counts churn as having a cancel_month; the monthly rate is cancels divided by accounts active at the start of the month.
Not pitched at a CEO: opens with a long data-quality section and a dense table using terms like 'account-months' and 'n.m.', and the summary has nested analyst-level detail.
The summary has 5 top-level bullets, but one has 3 sub-bullets, and the response adds 6 data-quality bullets plus a table. Well beyond a summary of at most 5 bullets.
Suggests one chart: monthly churn rate for Pro at 49, Pro at 69 and Basic, with a marker at July and hollow markers where the sample is small.
Rates confidence as low and explains why: 20 Pro accounts and 11 cancels, only 5 accounts behind the September 60% figure, and price is mixed up with who stayed and who left.
